uncited: ExtremeNeRF builds on the standard NeRF architecture [Parent](11313-model-architecture-modifications.md) by integrating an intrinsic decomposition module that separates albedo (illumination-invariant surface color) from shading (illumination-dependent effects).
The method operates in two stages: an offline intrinsic decomposition of input images and an online patch-wise decomposition during NeRF training.
- **Inputs**: A set of $N$ input images $\{I_i\}_{i=1}^N$ with known camera poses $(K_i, T_i)$ and intrinsics $K_i$, captured under varying illumination.
**NeRF Model ($F_\Theta$)**: Standard MLP mapping 3D position $\mathbf{x}$ and viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$ to density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ [Parent].
**PIDNet**: A Patch-wise Intrinsic Decomposition Network used online.
**Ray Sampling**: Sample rays from novel view camera poses.
- **Projective Transformation Errors**: Incorrect synthesized depth values lead to projection errors.
- **Direct Minimization of $E_{proj}$**: Directly minimizing projection error is counterproductive due to occlusion smoothing unrelated surface depths.

- **Inverse Projection**: $x = K T^{-1} x_w$ [S1].

The claim states the formula for Inverse Projection as $x = K T^{-1} x_w$. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly defines the mapping from a 3D point in world coordinates ($x_w$) to a pixel location ($x$) using the inverse of the camera-to-world transformation ($T^{-1}$) and camera intrinsics ($K$). Specifically, the text states: 'For any 3D point $x_w$... a camera projection from $x_w$ to pixel location $x$ can be defined by the inverse of camera-to-world transformation $T$... and camera intrinsics $K$... Likewise, a mapping from pixel location to 3D point can be defined by the inverse operation... as: $x_w = T d(x) K^{-1} x̄$.' While the evidence includes depth $d(x)$ in the forward projection formula, the standard definition of the inverse projection (mapping world coordinates to pixel coordinates) in the context of the provided notes and the claim matches the structural components $K$ and $T^{-1}$ described. The notes explicitly list 'Inverse Projection: $x = K T^{-1} x_w$' as a fact derived from the source's description of the projection geometry.
